messenger_reliability.builder_why:
Every capability in the row is present and answers for itself: reliability.json exercises twenty-one of them against a real host over the wire and all twenty-one pass, including the four that only appear when something goes wrong — a kill mid-send that does not duplicate, twenty-six events queued offline and delivered gapless, a refusal kept out of the wire and delivered when asked again, and a second phone pairing making the first say so rather than polling with a key the host has forgotten.

Three findings from cycle 9 are closed on the artifacts. The blocking one — no thread row in any of the fifteen artifacts showing a sent or received message tied to what it answers — is answered in 13_messenger_states, which now carries `replies_on_the_glass` mapping a delivered row to the event it replies to, `leaving now. dont cut the end off before i get there`. The serious one — `401 GET /v1/events?after=14075&wait=20` in two of fifteen scene logs while the same files said `faults: 0` — is gone: both clips record `problems: []` and `refused: 0` over 298 rounds. The cause was a browser's transparent retry of an idempotent GET replaying its own nonce, so the replay window is spent on writes now and every refusal names the device it refused and the pairing it held. The refusal's reason reaches the person in the far phone's own words, and `sent`, `going` and `it would not go` are on one screen.

What is not fixed is the scroll, and it is the row's own named failure. Over the same fling as cycle 9 the rows built fell from 5,028 to 167, worst tick 3 — `Note.build` no longer subscribes to the scope, so a sync round no longer rebuilds every row on the glass, and that is confirmed twice on two captures. The shape did not move: 67 of the 300 fling frames cost over 400 ms of build, median 662, against 233 that cost 7 — and those 67 are exactly the frames that build rows, which puts a row at about 266 ms. Two captures agree within four per cent. I do not know what that 266 ms is. The test that was read as ruling the hand fonts out runs under `flutter test`, which passes `--use-test-fonts --disable-asset-fonts`, so it laid every paragraph out in a font with nothing to shape and could not have seen it either way; that is now the first thing the file says. An experiment that builds the same commit twice, with and without the alternates, and shoots the same fling against each, is what will answer it. Until it does this row sits at its floor: a person flinging a year-deep thread on this build meets frames that cost two thirds of a second to put together.

material_truth.builder_why:
The blocking finding is closed and it was overstated when it was made. Cycle 9's material critic measured the fold's panels at a median 2.1 grey levels of ramp and called them flat images being transformed; the completeness pass re-measured the same clip in the same window and got 11.31. On this capture's packed frames a panel's centre column ramps 56 to 64 grey levels end to end with a 25-level step at the crease, because the fold now bends about a 2.2 mm arc with a flap that keeps turning over its own length rather than hinging.

The serious one that was not overstated is the one nobody had named: **a hole in the desk beside every sheet**. A coherence critic measured 758 pixels under luma 30 at one chip's edge in 12_search, minimum 4.3, against a desk reading 84 to 103 either side. It was two faults in one place — the paper's tear is nine-sliced and the baked contact shadow under it was stretched with BoxFit.fill, so on a piece far from the render's proportions the two stopped coinciding, and what came out from under the paper is black at alpha 255 over a third of every one of those assets. Nine-sliced and tinted to the warm shadow now. tools/check/holes.py measures the ring three to twelve pixels outside every sheet, with a control that is the fault drawn by hand (300 of its 600 pixels caught) and a control that is the densest writing in the set (0). Nine of seventeen stills had one; all ten pass now, nine reading zero, and the desk beside a sheet reads 34 to 48.

The app knows how big a millimetre is. Every stock is printed at a known pitch and every piece drew it at whatever scale that piece turned out to be; a piece takes a window of its stock at the stock's own density now, and the stocks were re-rendered so a full-width piece fits inside one. The ruled pitch across the set went from 61.5–178.5 device pixels to 70.9–132.0, a ratio of 1.86 — and the library's own rulings imply 1.74, because lined is 8.0 mm, graph 5.0, spiral 7.0, looseleaf and legal 8.7 and index 6.0. This check used to claim they were all eight, which made the fault look larger than it was; it says the right thing now. flat.py finds no file with a flat fill except one window.

That window is why this is the floor and not above it. 04_moments' voice-note tile measures 0.017 grey levels of tooth, and the receipt stock it is cut from measures 0.82 to 1.45 at every scale it could be drawn at. The stock is not being drawn. My first explanation — that the shutter fired before it decoded — was wrong: the harness waits for the image cache now and the window is unchanged. The report records the smallest patch of a stock any piece took so the next capture says what is happening. Half the tear library is still under 2 px rms of contour and the writing still sits a third of a pitch off the rules; both are measured in the evidence rather than argued away.

emotional_transmission.builder_why:
Two of cycle 9's three serious findings are answered on the artifacts.

The gesture that produces a feeling can be seen. A critic stepped frames 68 to 105 of 15_authored_feeling and found the object simply lifting off the grid and flying, with no press, hold or pressure affordance in any frame. A hold was added after that and it still could not be seen: 42 consecutive frames of this clip were byte-identical, exactly the run where a finger is put on `pigeon` and held, because the hold grows the intensity over 1.8 seconds and nothing asked for a repaint while the driven clock advanced. One frame of the run repeats now.

The non-haptic substitute is a knock rather than a bounce. The same critic measured the whole-page translation in all 421 frames of 07 and found the horizontal component exactly zero in every one. It has a direction of the feeling's own and a turn under a quarter of a degree now, and haptics.json carries both per feeling so the number can be held against the frames rather than taken on trust. Sideways is never further than up, because a page that slides as far as it lifts is a swipe.

And a feeling somebody drew is ink: 91 distinct values inside its strokes with a standard deviation of 17.7, against 24 and 7.5 for flat colour with the same taper. Four of the built-ins are drawn marks rather than rendered props and every critic so far has written as though all thirty-four were props, which is why a mark made of six translucent rectangles sat on the hero through nine reviews.

The third serious finding stands and cannot be closed here: nothing in the evidence ever vibrated, and the reception scene is a Chromium banner on a Linux virtual display, which the log says plainly.

coherence.builder_why:
Mood and availability reach the everywhere-element. A critic drove `state mood restless` and `state availability heads_down` through 08 and neither moved the partner ribbon: only place did, so on Moments and Settings a reader got three of five signals and the two missing were the two that decide whether to write to somebody. They are words, so they go where the words are, and only when the line above is not already saying them.

Moments' other two lenses are in the set — `crops/04_moments_what_happened.png` and `crops/04_moments_what_we_felt.png` — against a critic's finding that 154 events behind one and 1,340 behind the other were on the glass nowhere. The module strips no longer print the same sentence twice within one block. The search chip that showed 758 pixels of hole is the shadow fault above and is gone.

One log held identically on two devices across a tailnet is still the run recorded in coldstart.json, dated and not reproducible here; its `later_check` says so with a timestamp rather than quietly standing. And no artifact shows a second platform, which is the absence this row cannot get past.

anti_goal.builder_why:
The voice check reads every literal in lib that could reach a screen rather than a fixed list of nine call sites — 525 strings against the 116 a code critic counted, with the rules named in the report and every string it passed listed so a reader can disagree with a particular one. Zero findings.

The page now puts the desk out for the eight-to-ten-second first launch instead of showing a flat brown rectangle, and the line on it is written on the wood in the hand and the colour the app uses for anything not on paper. It was a slip first — a rectangle of real stock with a drop shadow and square corners, which is the one shape this row exists to catch — and a test now refuses a box-shadow anywhere on that surface.

grain.json no longer declares a ceiling it does not gate on. What keeps this at its floor is the one flat window in 04_moments: it is simulated paper by the row's own definition, whatever its cause, and it is on an artifact.

declined.finding: the desk's across-grain to along-grain ratio is 5.49 against the check's own stated max_ratio of 3.6, and it reports ok: true
declined.reason: The contradiction was real and is fixed — the ratio is reported and not gated now, and the report says why in its own text. The ratio itself is declined as a measurement: a pore adds to the gradient across the grain as much as along it, so anisotropy cannot tell painted stripes from visible oak. Five renders moved it from 5.76 to 5.13 while the surface changed completely. What is gated is the share of spectral power above 35 per cent of Nyquist, which the desk passes at 1.83 with its pores in and 1.23 without them.

declined.finding: the hero should show photographs, voice notes, reactions and replies in one frame
declined.from: the brief's description of the artifact
declined.reason: Declined on arithmetic, and measured: the tightest stretch of the seeded year holding a photograph, a voice note, a feeling and a reaction is a feeling 253 points tall, a photograph 393 and a message 243 — 889 points into a viewport 784 deep. Four sheets is all that fits, against this artifact's own standard of eight notes on eight different tears, which is what the material row reads it at three hundred per cent for. No alignment or entry row changes that. The frame takes the eight sheets with a photograph and a voice note among them; 13_messenger_states is where a reaction and a delivered reply are photographed.
